necessary_context.content: K arms; at each t one arm is selected and only its reward X_t^k in [0,1] is observed. Its mean is mu_t^k. The mean path is independent of the realized sample path of past actions. The inspected formulation does not explicitly specify a complete temporal joint-independence assumption for all rewards; do not infer one from the seed.
necessary_context.name: Bandit feedback and mean path

necessary_context.content: V(mu;T)=sum_{t=1}^{T-1} max_{k=1,...,K}|mu_t^k-mu_{t+1}^k|; L(V_T)={mu in [0,1]^(K×T):V(mu;T)<=V_T}. Section 2 introduces a nondecreasing budget sequence with V_1=0, K V_t<=t and normalization V_2=2/K; Theorems 1–2 separately display the horizon budget range [1/K,T/K].
necessary_context.name: Temporal variation and uncertainty set

necessary_context.content: Policies are measurable functions of a random seed and past observed rewards, hence nonanticipating and allowed to randomize. mu_t^*=max_k mu_t^k. R^pi(mu,T)=sum_t mu_t^*−E^pi[sum_t mu_t^{pi_t}]; expectation includes reward and policy randomness. R^pi(V_T,T)=sup_{mu in L(V_T)}R^pi(mu,T); R^*(V_T,T)=inf_{pi in P}R^pi(V_T,T). The mean-path adversary is nonadaptive. This definition uses expected selected means exactly as on PDF p.8; no equivalence to expected realized rewards is asserted.
necessary_context.name: Admissible policies and dynamic regret
